significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(iii) predictive coupling: attacks from unseen families produce sufficiently anomalous internal computation that a "mechanistic anomaly detector trained only on benign activations" outperforms supervised harmful-content classifiers, with SAE "feature-co-activation anomalies" more discriminative than raw activations. This fixes expectations across attack families and establishes a consequential behavioral regularity and internal correlate, but not a causal mechanism explaining why jailbreaks succeed; HarmBench (Mazeika et al., 2024) and JailbreakBench (Chao et al., 2024) make cross-attack robustness a concrete evaluation concern. Verified false is also informative because it would reject the generic premise that novel misuse reliably "looks weird" internally relative to benign computation, although it would not rule out narrower anomaly signals; true and false are distinguishable because the claim specifies comparative detection and representation-ordering predictions. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: generic mechanistic LLM safety does not imply benign-only detection, unseen-family generalization, or the predicted feature-versus-activation ordering, making this sharper than the topic's median probe-based hypothesis.

reach.justification: The named handle is a benign-only "mechanistic anomaly detector" producing activation- or SAE-feature anomaly scores; it is ex ante because it can flag an unseen jailbreak before its output is accepted, permitting runtime gating rather than merely explaining a completed failure. Re-extraction and threshold calibration would be needed for each model, but the substantive conclusion predicts a transferable relation—novel attacks score as more anomalous and benign-only detection beats supervised classification—rather than merely supplying a procedure with no expectation about the next setting; its asserted scope covers unseen attack families but not all harms, architectures, or training regimes. The likely downstream users include safety auditors and deployment operators who can gate suspicious requests, aligning with the operational defense role represented by Llama Guard (Inan et al., 2023), though no outside-AI uptake is claimed. The topic-substitution check fails to retain the score: the broad safety topic alone hands over no ex-ante anomaly score or benign-only gating rule, whereas this claim does.
